Our story

Rooted in the Free State for more than a century

Stephen's Nurseries was started around 1920 by my grandmother. My father joined the business when he came back from the war in 1947, and later took it over. I worked for him on and off for a few years, worked for other nurseries, and earned a diploma in Horticulture from Cape Technikon.

I took over the business in 1989. We still grow and make everything we sell, right here on the farm.

From the grower's notebook

A century of tips, one season at a time

Small notes from a third-generation grower. On the real site these become seasonal posts that bring in visitors from Google.

Summer

Water deep, not often

New grasses and shrubs love a deep soak twice a week far more than a little splash every day.

Winter

Plant fruit trees while they sleep

Dormant fruit trees settle in quickly and are ready to burst into blossom in spring.

All year

Soak concrete pots first

Give a new concrete pot a good soak before planting, and your plants will thank you.
